holidays.name: National Hanging Out Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble clothesline. People are encouraged to skip the electric dryer and let their laundry flap in the breeze. The day is meant to show that sunshine and fresh air do a fine job of drying clothes, and that sheets can smell like a spring meadow.
holidays.origin: The day was promoted by Project Laundry List, an advocacy group founded by Alexander Lee. It campaigns for the right to air-dry clothes and for energy-saving habits.
holidays.funFact: Some neighborhoods and homeowners' associations in the U.S. have restricted outdoor clotheslines, which sparked 'right to dry' laws in several states.

holidays.name: National Garlic Day
holidays.description: A day for people who think every dish needs more garlic. Roast it, mash it into butter, or toss it on pizza. Just share the breath with fellow garlic lovers.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is popular with foodies and garlic fans.
holidays.funFact: Garlic is a relative of onions, leeks and chives. It has been cultivated for thousands of years, and ancient Egyptian records mention it.

holidays.name: Bicycle Day
holidays.description: A day that marks one of the most famous bike rides in science history. Swiss chemist Albert Hofmann pedaled home through Basel after an unexpected experience with a compound he had synthesized, and the ride became a legend in pop culture and the history of science.
holidays.origin: On April 19, 1943, Hofmann deliberately took LSD for the first time in his laboratory. Wartime restrictions meant he cycled home, and the date has been remembered as Bicycle Day ever since.
holidays.funFact: Hofmann had first synthesized LSD in 1938. He only discovered its effects in 1943, after he accidentally absorbed a tiny amount a few days before the bike ride.
